rigChains.reason: 2026-10-11 lane B rig surgery (lane C rig_chain, h3_mammoth_upg_alt recipe): the trunk rode the Head bone rigidly, so the DEF trunk lift (Mouseover, g01 trumpet) and reach (AttackFront g12) could only be faked by tipping the head. A 6-bone chain along this mesh's own trunk centreline (traced from the head-weighted |x|<0.21 shell) takes the trunk's vertices; tusks (|x| > 0.15 below z 0.45), cheeks (|x| > 0.21), mouth (y > -0.6 from z 0.45, lips y > -0.68 above z 0.82: the trunk's own inner surface sits just in front of the mouth, and a wider mouth box left it behind as a hanging curtain) and forehead (z > 0.98) excluded; below z 0.95 the web faces bridging the trunk to the tusks, cheeks and mouth are split off and stay with the head.

glbPatch.reason: lane B 2026-10-11 authenticity: the DEF mammoth throws its head and trunk up and forward in AttackFront (f3-f6) and lifts it in Mouseover (f4-f9); the capture kept the head level in both. Neck + Head pitch the head up so the tusks and trunk swing out (as on h3_mammoth_upg_alt). The DEF trunk lift and reach ride a 6-bone trunk chain (rig_chain rig surgery, 2026-10-11) 2026-10-12 lane B tusk follow-up (mesh surgery pre-approved): the reach showed the left tusk in shards and a dark fleck under the trunk. The Meshy auto-rig had skinned the left tusk and cheek to the left foreleg they rest against, and a small patch of the left forefoot to Head. tusk_c2 surgery cuts the head side off the foreleg; the tusk table puts both tusks rigid on Head, mirrors the right cheek's skin onto the left and gives the forefoot patch its neighbours' weights; the head/neck skin is re-solved against every gated pose on the new mesh (tusk_reach_weights, replacing the old neck table), and a whole-body strain limiter covers the reach and walk clips.
